Special tray designer · Gothic arch integration

1Scan input

Load the scan and set the arch.

A separate workflow for both jaws. Each jaw gets a full-coverage bite plate with a wax-rim-shaped platform, and a full-arch tracer plate that sits on the rim on locating pins. Closed together, the two bite plates stack with the tracer between them: the flat tracing plate on one, the pin plate on the other.

Upper scannot loaded
Lower scannot loaded

If the scans were taken in the bite position they are used as they are. If not (scanned separately), the second scan is turned to face the first and placed opposite it over the arch, at the gap you set; the tracer then records the real jaw relation. The first scan you load is designed first; switch jaws with the Upper / Lower buttons at the top of this panel.

Load the edentulous / partially dentate cast or impression scan (STL or PLY, mm).

2Insertion axis & alignment

Check the scan sits tissue side up; adjust the insertion axis if needed.

Look straight at the fitting surface along the path the tray will seat, then set the axis. Red = undercut from this direction.

3-point: click three points on the occlusal / ridge plane (e.g. both tuberosities/retromolar pads and incisive area).

Fine tune
Changing the axis clears painting, margin and tray.

3Relief, stops & post damoptional

Relief, stops and post dam, if you want them.

Relief adds extra spacer (tori, incisive papilla, flabby ridge, mental foramen). Stop brings the tray into contact locally. Erase removes either.

4.0
45%
Tissue stops (automatic)

Found from the scan inside your tray margin (draw that first). They are painted into the Stop layer, so the brush can move, enlarge or erase them; pressing again replaces the last set. Stops act on a special tray only: a record base has no spacer.

Post dam (upper)

Mark the landmarks on the scan (best checked in the mouth first), then press Place post dam. Drag a landmark on the scan to move it; a placed post dam follows.

Bra-shaped: lines from the papilla to each hamular notch find the soft junction of ridge and hard palate; the bra's top sits just behind the rugae; the posterior border runs between the notches, behind the foveae. The inner border mirrors the outer, centred on a line square to the posterior border. The cast is beaded along the posterior border and the inner border (deeper at the sides, ½ mm over the midline and at the top) and feathered from the bead out to the bra's border. Relief inside is optional: advised over tori, not for deep vaults.

Traditional: a bead along the posterior border from notch to notch behind the foveae, deepest at the sides and shallow over the midline, feathered forward like a butterfly.

0

Click along the vibrating line, from one hamular notch across to the other (3–5 points); it is drawn as a smooth curve through them. Deepest along the line, feathered forward over the soft palate (further at the sides, less over the midline, where the mucosa is thin) and short behind. It is carved into the model before the tray or base is built, so it comes out as smooth as the rest of the palate: a record base fits it; a special tray carries the same bead on its fitting surface (the spacer stays), so the impression presses a little more on the post dam area.

4Blockout modelcheck

Check the blockout preview; adjust only if needed.

Undercuts seen from the insertion axis are filled automatically (height-map blockout). A draft angle tapers the blockout walls so the tray seats and withdraws cleanly.

5Tray margin

Draw the outline round the sulcus.
1 · Teeth the tray rests on

Click each tooth the tray should rest on, on its biting edge or chewing surface; click its dark mark to drop it. The tray covers it from the tips down, close fitting, like a splint.

0
2 · Flange over each gap

Draw the flange outline round the edentulous area with the margin tool below, letting it run up onto the capped teeth beside the gap so the parts join. It may run past the edge of the model onto the grey skirt. For a second gap, press Add another flange and draw again. The flange uses the spacer, thickness and border from step 6.

Click points around the tray border on the scan, then click the first point to close. After generating you can still edit it from any step with Edit margin (top bar): drag points, click the line to add one, double-click to delete, Ctrl/⌘+Z to undo.

0open
Suction outline

Mark a few landmarks and the outline is drawn for you from the scan, following the suction-effective rules; edit it afterwards like any margin. Drag a landmark on the scan to move it: the outline redraws itself until you edit the margin by hand.

Lower: the whole retromolar pad is covered and the line comes up to the pad at its buccal root (clear of the sinew string). Over the buccal shelf it runs at the bottom of the fold, and from the premolars forward it stops short of the fold. Lingually it goes 2–3 mm past the mylohyoid ridge into the retromylohyoid fossa, then swings up in an S onto the most convex part of the lingual slope and runs to the lingual frenum. It goes to the floor of the sulcus only when the ridge is badly resorbed. Frena you mark get a notch. Where the scan shows no clear fold, the line goes where the slope flattens out.

Upper: the line covers the tuberosities and runs into the hamular notches, and across the palate just behind the vibrating line (behind the post dam's posterior border if you have placed one). It stops about 2 mm short of the fold buccally and 3 mm labially, and frena you mark get a wider notch.

Click along the mucogingival junction (or your pencilled outline). The tray is an offset of the surface inside this line only, so its periphery finishes exactly on the line — on walls as well as flat areas.

6Tray settings & generate

Choose tray or record base, then generate.

Special tray: spaced off the tissue, borders tapered and kept short.

The border is made thick over the buccal shelf and in the sublingual fold (where the spongy tissue seals), thin in the retromylohyoid fossa, and thin over the retromolar pads so the tongue and cheek can meet above them. The buccal surface from the second molar back to the pad is made concave or convex as chosen; the tongue root, the tongue space in front and the incisor surface are made concave. The retromolar pads come from the suction-outline landmarks (step 5), or from the ends of the ridge if none are marked.

The tray is a true 3-D offset of the blocked-out surface inside your margin line. Its border is a fully rounded bead that follows the line in one smooth sweep, as thick as the border-edge value; the tray tapers down to it. Fit surface stays locked; smoothing only affects the outer surface.

7Handle, holes & IDoptional

Handle, holes and an ID label, if you want them.

Fills the flanges with perforations (size and spacing as for painted holes below), clear of the caps and the border. Paint more or remove them with the hole tools.

Handle

Straight: a bar leaving the tray at the elevation angle. Stepped: rises off the ridge, then turns forward so it clears the lip. Stub: a short upright grip.

Finger rests
0

Blocks on the ridge crest to seat a lower tray with the fingers — click once each side, usually in the premolar–molar region. They start along the arch.

Move or turn a handle or rest

Click a handle or finger rest on the tray to select it, as with the Gothic arch plate: drag the arrows to move it (it stays on the tray surface) or switch to Rotate and drag the rings to spin and tilt it.

Retentive loops (neutral zone)
0

Upright loops on a lower tray or base to hold the neutral zone impression material. Click on the ridge where a group should sit: it is centred there and runs along the ridge. “Front + both sides” replaces them with three groups: one at the front and one over each molar region. Height, width, count and thickness apply to every group.

Holes (perforations)

Drag over the tray to lay holes in an even pattern at this spacing; go over an area again and nothing doubles up. A single click with a small brush adds one hole. Holes go straight through the tray wall and keep clear of the border, the handle and an embedded plate.

Windows

An opening right through the tray, for example over a flabby ridge. Click round the area on the tray and click the first point again to close; the outline is smoothed. Undo removes the last point, or the last window.

ID text

Text is projected along the insertion axis — place it on a flat outer area (palate or occlusal).

8Gothic arch integration

Add the Gothic arch component.

Pick a component, set it up from the occlusal plane, then choose how it joins the tray.

Arrangement

Occlusal plane & pin position

Mark three points on the scan: one second-premolar region, the other second-premolar region, then the midline at the front. Use cusp tips and the incisal edge on a dentate arch, the ridge crest on an edentulous one.

0 if you marked cusp tips. On a ridge crest, enter the height the occlusal plane should stand above it (the rim height).

3 · Rim

Like a wax rim: the labial face of the rim at the midline stands this far in front of the ridge crest (about 8 upper, 6 lower), for lip support. It may stand up to 3 mm past the outline; there it is at most 4 mm deep, so the border and sulcus stay clear.

The rim stops sooner where the bite plate climbs towards the plane (over the pads). At the back it is centred over the ridge within the outline.

Sets the height of the occlusal plane for you. With one jaw built, its rim stands this high at its lowest; with both, the plane goes midway between what each jaw needs, so both rims stand equally high.

Halfway between the two scans, then moved so both rims stand the same height (the pin side needs the pin gap as well as its plate).

Off: the palate or tongue space stays open under the plate. On: the plate is supported all over where the bite plate lies beneath it (a channel is left for the pin).

4 · Plates

How far the pin projects from the pin plate to the tracing plate: the plates stand this far apart, touching only at the pin.

The hex-nut plate is built into the pin plate with its nut and thread exactly as designed. Auto picks the narrow plate, else the compact one, whichever fits; if none does, its ends are trimmed to the outline, well clear of the thread.

Both plates are horseshoes along the rim with a bridge across the middle: the pin plate carries the hex-nut plate there, the tracing plate a tracing table.

5 · Build and check

After the tracing, fix the disc on the tracing plate with its hole over the apex of the arrow point; the pin drops into it and holds the jaws for the record.

Paired trays (both jaws)

For a tracer that works between an upper and a lower tray at the bite: load the opposing scan in step 1 (taken in the bite position), set the plane here, add the rims, then save the set-up. When you design the other tray, load its scan with this one as the opposing scan and use the set-up: it gets the same occlusal plane and matching rims, and is told how far its pin must reach.

A flat-topped block over each first-molar region, standing up to the occlusal plane, so the two trays meet in the bite for the closed-mouth impression. Each rim sits on its own tray on two pegs and lifts off for the tracing. They are kept clear of the tracer plate.

After the tracing, fix the disc on the registration plate with its hole over the apex of the arrow point; the pin drops into the hole and holds the jaws in that relation for the record.

Position
—
—
—
Connection to tray

One piece, not removable: the plate stands at the height you set (its face on the occlusal plane) on solid supports that rise from the tray only where the tray lies under it, so the tongue space stays open. Default for a registration plate on a mandibular tray or base.

One piece, not removable: the plate is sunk into the tray until its face is flush, the vault under it is filled, and the fill is blended down to the tray so nothing stands proud (as in Qu et al. 2019, Fig 4B). Default for a flat registration plate on a maxillary tray or base.

Thinned from the tray side; the working face, its holes and the central thread are left exactly as designed (the thread keeps its full length inside a collar).

Default for the supporting pin plate (the hex-nut plate that carries the registration pin). Removable, held the traditional way: plain pins stand on short posts on the tray and pass into plain holes in the plate, which only locate it. Seat the plate on the posts and hold it with sticky wax or adhesive; to remove it, warm the wax or break the bond and lift straight off. No slots, clips or detents. The central thread and nut seat are never cut.

With existing holes, each pin is sized to its hole (hole Ø less the clearance) and the plate is left as designed; the pin Ø above applies to auto-placed pins, whose holes are drilled straight through the plate. Auto stops pins 0.3 mm below the working face.

Detected plate holes

Channel keeps the hole clear straight through the connector and tray (e.g. so the pin screw can wind right through). Hole geometry itself is never modified.

9Export

Download the parts.

Untick to export with the insertion axis as +Z (handy for setting up the print).

In Embedded / Raised / Wall modes the plate and tray are one watertight piece (thread untouched) — the first button gives you that single part. In Locating pins mode export the tray and the plate separately so the plate stays removable; it is held on the pins with sticky wax or adhesive.
